summary:
Wonersh is a village and civil parish in Surrey’s Waverley district, 3 to 6 miles southeast of Guildford and 28 miles southwest of London. The parish includes Shamley Green and Blackheath, and lies within the Surrey Hills National Landscape. Its service-sector economy reflects its position in the London commuter belt.

Mesolithic flint tools and the pre-Conquest core of St John the Baptist’s Church indicate early settlement. In the 16th and 17th centuries, Wonersh prospered through the production of blue cloth known as Guildford Blue. The parish also had six medieval manors and several historic charitable endowments.

The landscape includes commons, woodland and hills, with elevations from 39 metres to 207 metres. Winterfold Wood and Heath covers much of the southeast. The parish has three conservation areas and numerous listed buildings, including Grade I-listed Great Tangley Manor and the Grade II*-listed Dower House and Barnett Hill.

Local facilities include a co-operative village shop and post office, pub, sports green and community groups. The B2128 crosses the village; Shalford is the nearest railway station.
